lines.text: Today you become a reporter! You will learn to ask great questions and give clear answers.
What asks about a thing.
Where asks about a place, and when asks about a time.
Who asks about a person, why asks for a reason, and how asks about the way.
Put the question word at the start.
Then add do or does, or is or are.
What do you like?
You do not always need a long answer.
To do you like mangoes, say yes, I do, or no, I don’t.
To what is your favourite colour, just say blue, or my favourite colour is blue.
A follow-up question keeps a chat going.
If your friend says I like cricket, ask why do you like it, or who is your favourite player?
It shows you are really listening.
Listen to Riya interview her friend Arjun.
Riya asks, What is your favourite game? Arjun says, Cricket!
Riya asks a follow-up question. Why do you like it? Because I love batting.
Then she asks, When do you play? Arjun says, every evening, in the park.
Riya used three different question words. Can you name them? What, why and when.
Some questions only need a yes or a no. Do you like mangoes? Yes, I do.
Questions with what, why and how ask you to tell more.
Good reporters ask tell me more questions, because the answers are more interesting.
A great reporter listens to the whole answer before speaking again.
Nod and say oh, nice, or really, to show you are interested.
At the end, always say thank you for talking to me.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
